corrected_content.problem:
Given that the differential equation
$y^{″} - 6y^{′} + 34y = 0$

has the general solution
$y = e^{3x}(P\cos 5x + Q\sin 5x)$,

solve the initial value problem
$$
\displaystyle y^{″} - 6y^{′} + 34y = 0, y(0) = 5, y^{′}(0) = 10.
$$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
The characteristic roots are $3\pm5\mathrm{i},$ so
$$
y=e^{3x}(P\cos5x+Q\sin5x).
$$
The first condition gives $P=5.$ Differentiating,
$$
y'=3e^{3x}(P\cos5x+Q\sin5x)+e^{3x}(-5P\sin5x+5Q\cos5x).
$$
Using $y'(0)=10$ gives $3P+5Q=10,$ hence $Q=-1.$ Therefore,
$$
y=e^{3x}(5\cos5x-\sin5x).
$$
